text:
Maya: quick heads-up — during a customer demo I hit inconsistent auth warnings between CLI/sdks. thought we already unified envs but found three different behaviors. short thread to decide an action plan.

Maya: repro summary: user has both REDWOOD_ORG_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY set. CLI uses REDWOOD_API_KEY, go-sdk picks ORG, ruby-sdk emits no warning and silently uses ORG.

Tom: ugh. can you paste minimal logs? even a short snippet is fine.

Maya: logs: \\n[cli] INFO Using API key from REDWOOD_API_KEY\\n[go-sdk] INFO Using API key from REDWOOD_ORG_KEY\\n[ruby-sdk] INFO Using API key from REDWOOD_ORG_KEY\\n[ruby-sdk] WARN no deprecation logged

Ravi: that suggests parity drift. we added REDWOOD_API_KEY midway but kept the older vars for backwards compat. we should have a single canonical var.

Maya: agreed. I think UX wants: (1) canonical REDWOOD_API_KEY, (2) if older vars present log a single-time WARN pointing to migration doc, (3) if both canonical and legacy present, prefer canonical and warn about ambiguity.

Tom: +1. what about org vs project scoping? some customers rely on org-scoped keys for billing separation. do we lose that if we switch?

Ravi: we don't need to remove scoping: canonical name can be REDWOOD_API_KEY but accept a suffix pattern for project-level like REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT or guidance to use explicit headers for scope. but that's confusing. alternative: keep REDWOOD_API_KEY and a REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID env var to indicate scope.

Maya: devs will hate too many envs. simpler: REDWOOD_API_KEY always contains the final key; if user wants project-scoped, the token itself should be a project key and metadata is read from the key. so we don't need separate project env names.

Tom: makes sense. plan then: deprecate REDWOOD_ORG_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY in favor of REDWOOD_API_KEY across SDKs and CLI. Implementation steps?

Ravi: propose ship plan:
- SDKs (js, py, go, ruby): on init check for REDWOOD_API_KEY first; if not present, check legacy vars but emit a single WARN with link to migration guide (only once per process). if both canonical + legacy present, prefer canonical and emit WARN about legacy ignored.
- CLI: same behavior but also return exit code 0 with a printed NOTICE for interactive installs.
- Sample apps & quickstart: update quickstarts to set REDWOOD_API_KEY only, add a "troubleshooting" snippet for legacy users.
- Telemetry: optional event when WARN fired (opt-in) to measure rollout.

Maya: timeline? I need docs updated before next week's customer onboarding.

Ravi: I can PR sdk-go and sdk-ruby fixes in 48h. js and py teams might need 72h. CLI patch might be tiny. Docs update can land concurrently once sdk warnings exist.

Tom: can we add tests to the sdk parity-suite? e.g., set multiple env combos and assert consistent precedence and that WARN fires. This will prevent future regressions.

Ravi: yes I'll add a cross-sdk integration test in our infra repo that runs all SDKs in a docker harness. we'll assert the environment outputs match.

Maya: one more UX ask: when we warn, include an inline snippet showing current env values redacted, e.g., "Found REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=org_***. To migrate, set REDWOOD_API_KEY=..." That helps users triage. Keep it secure ofc.

Tom: agreed. also add a link to CLI command to migrate: `redwood auth migrate --from-org REDWOOD_ORG_KEY --to REDWOOD_API_KEY` (CLI team can implement a helper).

Ravi: assign owners: Ravi -> sdk-go/sdk-ruby tests + warning; Lina (js) -> sdk-js fix; Priya (py) -> sdk-py fix; Tom -> cli helper + quickstart updates; Maya -> docs + migration guide. I'll open tracker tickets and label P1 for onboarding friction.

cli-bot: Created ticket RDW-4532: "Unify API key env var across SDKs and CLI" (assignee: Ravi).

DocsBot: New docs draft created: "Auth env var migration" (link in #docs once ready).

Maya: thanks. small follow-up: do we want to add a deprecation header to sampleapps (banner in README) for one release cycle?

Tom: yes, add a short banner: "Using legacy env vars? See migration guide" and link it.

Ravi: ok I'll land the sdk changes behind a minor release with WARNs. Then schedule a breaking removal in 1.0 roadmap (announce in changelogs and console).

Maya: awesome. ping #devex when PRs are up and I'll review the docs. thanks folks. ✅
